# [TASK] Spike: Vosk English/German model selection for accent robustness

## Task
Spike: evaluate Vosk model options for English and German for accent/dialect
robustness within the $0/offline constraint.

## Scope
Research and a documented decision — not the integration itself (that's Task
#212).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] English options compared (current small model vs. `vosk-model-en-us-0.22` or similar) against a quick accented-speech smoke test — compared against published WER benchmarks (LibriSpeech/TED-LIUM/call-center) instead, since this environment has no network egress to the model-hosting domain and #215's fixture didn't exist yet (`docs/architecture/adr/021-vosk-bilingual-model-selection.md`, Context section)
- [x] German model options identified and one selected: `vosk-model-small-de-0.15`, over `vosk-model-small-de-zamia-0.3`, `vosk-model-de-0.21`, and `vosk-model-de-tuda-0.6-900k` (`docs/architecture/adr/021-vosk-bilingual-model-selection.md`)
- [x] Download size and runtime RAM cost documented for each candidate (`docs/architecture/adr/021-vosk-bilingual-model-selection.md`'s comparison table; the ADR also flags that #212 must measure actual combined RSS rather than trust disk-size figures alone)
- [x] Decision and rationale written up before #212 starts (`docs/architecture/adr/021-vosk-bilingual-model-selection.md`)

## Estimate
**Hours:** 4

## Notes
**Decision:** switch English from `vosk-model-small-en-us-0.15` to `vosk-model-en-us-0.22-lgraph` (128MB), and add `vosk-model-small-de-0.15` (45MB) as the first German model.

Full-size models (1.8GB to 4.4GB) are ruled out for both languages — they wouldn't fit ai-service's 768Mi memory / 512Mi ephemeral-storage limits even alone, let alone with a second language resident.
